Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa, branch feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component.

Score Step 1 of the SFCC-236 build (ZimmSlideIndicator molecule) against the six axes. This is round 1 — no prior rework has happened on this step.

Files: overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSlideIndicator/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx,index.test.tsx,zimmSlideIndicator.css.ts} + 2-line diff in overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts.

## Orchestrator verdict: IN SCOPE
5 files total, exactly the manifest, every named pass criterion evidenced against real test runs (12/12 own tests, 24/24 recipeParts.test.ts, 6/6 recipeGuards.test.ts, 127/127 theme/index.test.tsx, tsc/eslint/audit:tokens all clean). No under- or over-delivery. One non-blocking note: the plan document's own §7 loop table has a stale line (still says "aria-hidden root") that contradicts §4a's revision two sections earlier — this is a planning-doc inconsistency, not an implementer error; the Implementer correctly followed the resolved §4a text, not the stale §7 summary.

## Tester findings (four real mutation-and-revert cycles performed, all confirmed working as evidence)

1. **🟡 CONFIRMED, UNIFORM** — `zimmSlideIndicator.css.ts:48`: `background: isActive ? 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)' : ...` uses a `text.*` semantic token on a `background` property. The correct token, `var(--zimm-color-bg-05)`, resolves to the byte-identical value (`grey[900]`) and is already used for exactly this purpose elsewhere (`footer.css.ts:33`). Zero-visual-diff, semantically-correct fix available. UNIFORM because the identical mistake already exists in `zimmButton.css.ts:42` (pre-existing, not this step's fault, but this step repeats the category of error).

2. **🔴 flagged "must-fix" by Tester, but it's an infrastructure/testing-gap finding, not a defect in shipped behaviour** — the component's double-`useMultiStyleConfig` call pattern (`styles` for isActive:false, `activeStyles` for isActive:true) creates two proven blind spots via actual mutation testing: (a) `recipeParts.test.ts`'s regex only recognises the literal `styles.` prefix, so a part read only via `activeStyles.X` would go undetected if ever mis-declared; (b) `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s exhaustive-branch walker only varies 5 hardcoded boolean prop names (not this recipe's actual `isActive` key), so a planted bare-token-key violation on the `isActive:true` branch was never caught by the walk. Tester notes the SAME two gaps already pre-exist for `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts`'s `selected` prop (by inspection, not re-tested) — so this is a pre-existing shared-test-infrastructure limitation, not unique to this PR. Tester's own recommendation: extracting a `ZimmSlideDot` atom (mirroring how `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` delegates per-item styling to a `ZimmColourSwatch` atom, which calls `useMultiStyleConfig` once per its own mount) would sidestep both gaps for free, using established precedent — but that is an architecture change beyond what Step 1's manifest asked for (4 files, no new atom), and `recipeGuards.test.ts`/`recipeParts.test.ts` are shared, Tier-2/cross-cutting test files that a single-component step should not unilaterally modify.

3. **🟡 CONFIRMED, UNIFORM** — `index.stories.tsx:5`: `title: 'Elements/ZimmSlideIndicator'`. Per `.claude/rules/components.md`'s categorisation table and the component's own JSDoc ("product card's image carousel"), this is PDP/commerce-specific — every sibling PDP component (`ZimmColourSwatch`, `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`, `ZimmProductContent`, etc.) files under `Commerce/`. Should be `Commerce/ZimmSlideIndicator`. UNIFORM because the sibling arrow-buttons component (same image-carousel context, built in a later step) risks the same miscategorisation if this file is used as its reference.

4. **🟡 PLAUSIBLE, cannot verify in jsdom** — the root's `aria-label` is static, not a live region. Since this indicator's own premise is reflecting position during a touch swipe (a gesture that never moves focus to/through the `role="group"` container), a screen-reader user may not hear position updates in real time — `aria-label` is announced on focus/entry, not on mutation. Tester is explicit this is beyond the letter of the step's pass criteria (which only required "not aria-hidden" + "a real computed name," both satisfied) but is in the spirit of the component's stated sole-position-signal premise. No live-device verification was possible.

5. **🟡 CONFIRMED absent** — code comments in `index.tsx`, `zimmSlideIndicator.css.ts`, and `index.test.tsx` cite "SFCC-236 plan §4a" / "§4" as the source of the touch-only/never-aria-hidden requirement. Tester searched `.docs/` and all project memory files exhaustively and found no such document in the repo — the plan lives outside the repo at `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-236/plan.md` (deliberately, per the build skill's own rule: "never write run state into the repo"). The comment's citation is therefore uncitable to a future repo-only reader (e.g. a code reviewer with no access to that external path) — this project's own "Doc integrity"/"provenance not proximity" principle wants a comment to cite something reachable, not a private planning artifact.

6. **🔵 note, CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF** — test suite never calls `rerender()`, only fresh `render()`. Tester independently wrote and ran a throwaway re-render probe (3 cases) confirming correctness, then deleted it. Not a functional defect, minor coverage gap.

7. Tester also noted the Implementer's own self-report overstated one thing (claimed a "raw literal exception for colour" that doesn't actually exist in the shipped code — the real code is cleaner than described, using token vars throughout with a provisional-pairing comment instead). Not a defect, just a self-report accuracy note.

## Your job
Score all six axes (whatever this project's zm-scorer six axes are — apply your own rubric). Weigh in particular: is finding #1 (cheap, zero-visual-diff, confirmed) and #3 (cheap, confirmed, wrong category) worth a REWORK round given they're trivial fixes fully within this step's own files? Is finding #2 (the testing-infrastructure blind spot) something to report-and-defer rather than block on, given fixing it means touching shared/cross-cutting Tier 2 test files outside this step's manifest? Is finding #5 (uncitable comment reference) worth requiring a fix, given this project's explicit "provenance not proximity" rule?

Give PASS or REWORK. If REWORK, give the Implementer a SPECIFIC, bounded instruction — not "address the tester's findings" — naming exactly which findings to fix and which to leave for Marcel's report, and confirm the fix scope stays inside the same 5 files (no new atom, no touching recipeGuards.test.ts/recipeParts.test.ts).

1	import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
2	
3	/**
4	 * Recipe for the touch-only PDP/card image position indicator — a 1px hairline strip, one
5	 * segment per image, the current position picked out by colour. Figma node 40002536:7957
6	 * ("Slide indicator") confirms only the strip's height (1px, flush to the image's bottom edge)
7	 * and that it is NOT floating dots; per-segment width/gap and the exact colour pairing are not
8	 * broken out in the export handed to this step, so both are treated as open design decisions
9	 * (documented below) rather than invented pixel-for-pixel guesses — same precedent as
10	 * zimmColourSwatchGroup's `pagination` part leaving an unconfirmed inter-button gap at the flex
11	 * default rather than inventing one.
12	 *
13	 * Two parts:
14	 *   - `root` — the full-width flex strip, exactly `--zimm-scale-025` (1px) tall.
15	 *   - `dot` — one equal-width segment per image (despite the part name, this renders as a
16	 *     rectangle in a hairline, not a circular dot — the name matches this component's
17	 *     already-agreed contract, not a literal shape description).
18	 */
19	export const ZimmSlideIndicator = {
20	  parts: ['root', 'dot'],
21	
22	  baseStyle: ({ isActive }: { isActive?: boolean }): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
23	    root: {
24	      display: 'flex',
25	      // Fluid, not a fixed Figma px width — matches the product card's own "fluid, not 288px"
26	      // rule (SFCC-236 plan §4): this strip always spans whatever width its image parent gives
27	      // it, rather than the specific 159.11px/99.44px bounding boxes the two sampled Figma
28	      // variants happened to measure at their own artboard widths.
29	      width: '100%',
30	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-025)', // 1px — the one dimension Figma confirms directly.
31	      // No confirmed inter-segment gap value in the export handed to this step — left at 0
32	      // (segments flush-adjacent) rather than invented, so the strip reads as one continuous
33	      // hairline with the active segment picked out by colour alone. Revisit if a designer
34	      // confirms a real gap value.
35	      gap: 0,
36	    },
37	
38	    dot: {
39	      // Equal-width segments filling the strip — no confirmed per-segment width ratio exists
40	      // to justify an unequal split (see root's own comment above).
41	      flex: '1 0 0',
42	      height: '100%',
43	      // Both colours derive from the same grey/900 primitive (see foundation/colour.ts's
44	      // `opacity` family), so "active" and "inactive" read as solid vs. dimmed versions of one
45	      // hairline colour rather than two unrelated tones — a reasonable placeholder pairing
46	      // pending UI-designer confirmation of the exact treatment (only the strip's geometry, not
47	      // its colour, is confirmed by the Figma export handed to this step).
48	      background: isActive ? 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)' : 'var(--zimm-color-opacity-40)',
49	    },
50	  }),
51	};

## Verification performed before scoring

I independently reproduced the Orchestrator's and Tester's numbers rather than taking them on faith:

- `npx vitest run` on all four affected test files: **12/12, 24/24, 6/6, 127/127 — 169/169 total, exact match** to the Orchestrator's claim.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean. `npx eslint` on the component folder + theme index: clean.
- `npm run audit:tokens`: zero findings anywhere in `zimmSlideIndicator/*` (one unrelated pre-existing violation in `footer.css.ts:20`, untouched by this diff).
- Read `theme/foundation/colour.ts`, `recipeGuards.test.ts`, `recipeParts.test.ts`, `zimmButton.css.ts`, and every `.stories.tsx` title in `ui-kits/` directly, rather than relying on the Tester's paraphrase.

---

## Per-axis table (most severe first)

| Axis | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Design fidelity** | **UNVERIFIED** | No visual checkpoint (Storybook render vs. Figma node `40002536:7957`) is evidenced anywhere in the Orchestrator's or Tester's account, and I have no Figma tool access in this session to run one myself. The component's own comments responsibly flag inter-segment gap and exact colour pairing as unconfirmed placeholders pending designer sign-off — good practice, but it documents the gap, it doesn't close it. Per this review's own rule, this cannot be marked PASS on green gates alone. |
| **Correctness** | **REWORK** | `tsc`/`eslint`/tests all green (reproduced myself). One CONFIRMED defect: `zimmSlideIndicator.css.ts:48` uses `var(--zimm-color-text-default)` (a `text.*` token) on a `background` property. I confirmed `text.default` and `background['05']` both resolve to `grey[900]`/`#191919` in `colour.ts` — zero visual diff, but the semantically correct token is `bg-05`, already used for this exact purpose in `footer.css.ts:33`. I also confirmed the Tester's "UNIFORM" claim: `zimmButton.css.ts:42` has the identical `bg: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)'` pattern pre-existing. — Separately, Tester's finding #2 (🔴) is a real, CONFIRMED test-harness blind spot (verified by reading `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s `PROP_COMBINATIONS`/`DEFAULT_STYLE_PROPS` directly: `isActive` is never a key there, so the `isActive:true` branch of the function-form `baseStyle` is never resolved by any of the 32 combos the guard walks; and `recipeParts.test.ts`'s `READ_RE` is a case-sensitive literal match on `styles`, so `activeStyles.dot` is structurally invisible to it). I'm not treating this as this step's Correctness blocker — see "report vs. block" below. |
| **Conformance** | **REWORK** | Styling hierarchy, recipe namespacing, and structure all hold (confirmed: `var(--zimm-*)` throughout, no bare token keys, no base-SFCC recipe collision, folder layout matches sibling molecules). One CONFIRMED defect: `index.stories.tsx:5` files under `Elements/` when every other PDP/commerce sibling in this tree (`ZimmColourSwatch`, `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`, `ZimmProductContent`, `ZimmProductMeta`, `ZimmProductPrice`, `ZimmProductStyleCode`, `ZimmProductDescription`, `ZimmProductName`, `ZimmProductModelInfo`, `ZimmPdpDrawer` — 10 components checked) files under `Commerce/` — confirmed by grepping every `.stories.tsx` title in `ui-kits/`. |
| **Completeness** | **REWORK** | Story present (5 named exports covering both sampled Figma variant sets), test present (12 tests covering count, active-segment, clamping, `count<=1`, a11y), ACs satisfied. One CONFIRMED defect: three comments (`index.tsx:26`, `index.test.tsx:91`, `zimmSlideIndicator.css.ts:27`) cite "SFCC-236 plan §4a"/"§4" as a source. I grepped `.docs/` recursively — no such artifact exists in the repo. I also compared against every other `§`-citation in the codebase (`TSD §12.1`, `testing.md §Layer-2`, Handover `button.md §focus`, `CSS Flexbox §4`) — all of those point at something a repo-only or company-wide reader can actually open (a spec, a repo file, a Confluence doc, a named design-handover package). "SFCC-236 plan §4a" points at a private, per-session file that is deliberately never committed anywhere — structurally different, not just a stricter case of the same thing. |
| **Pass criteria** | PASS | Touch-only rendering, never-`aria-hidden` root with a real computed name, index clamping, `count<=1` renders nothing — all evidenced by tests I ran myself, not asserted. |
| **Restraint** | PASS | Orchestrator gave IN SCOPE with no OVER/UNDER flag; I confirmed via `git status --short` that only the 4 new component files + the 2-line `theme/components/index.ts` diff are touched — nothing else. |

## Overall: REWORK (round 1 of 3)

---

## What I tried to falsify

- Reran the full test matrix myself rather than trusting the reported counts — got the identical 169/169 split across the four files, plus a clean `tsc`/`eslint`/`audit:tokens`.
- Traced `recipeGuards.test.ts` and `recipeParts.test.ts` source directly to check whether finding #2's mechanism claims actually hold, rather than trusting the Tester's account of their own mutation test. Confirmed both blind spots structurally: `DEFAULT_STYLE_PROPS` genuinely has no `isActive` key (so the `isActive:true` branch is never in any of the 32 walked combinations), and `READ_RE` is genuinely a case-sensitive literal match on `styles` that cannot see `activeStyles.dot`.
- Went one step further than either the Tester or Orchestrator: checked whether a **fourth option** exists for finding #2 beyond "touch shared test files" / "extract an atom" / "defer" — restructuring the recipe from a function-form `baseStyle({isActive})` to Chakra `variants: {active, inactive}` would make `collect()`'s unconditional `r.variants` walk see both branches, closing blind spot (b) without touching `recipeGuards.test.ts`/`recipeParts.test.ts` or adding a new atom. I'm deliberately **not** mandating this in round 1 — it's a real design-mechanism change nobody has vetted yet, not a same-file token/label swap — but it's worth putting in front of whoever picks up the follow-up ticket.
- Checked whether "zero-visual-diff" for finding #1 was actually true by reading the token source, not the Tester's assertion: `text.default` and `background['05']` are both literally `grey[900]` in `colour.ts`. Confirmed.
- Checked whether finding #3's categorisation call was a matter of taste or a real rule violation by grepping every sibling story title. It's not close — 10/10 genuinely PDP-adjacent siblings use `Commerce/`.
- Checked whether finding #5's citation is really different in kind from existing codebase practice, not just pickier — compared it against every other `§` citation in `overrides/`. It is different in kind: every existing one names something durably addressable; this one doesn't.
- Read the actual shipped `zimmSlideIndicator.css.ts` to check finding #7 — confirmed no raw literal exists anywhere in the file (only `var(--zimm-color-*)` references), so the self-report's claim doesn't match the delivered code.

## What I could not verify

- **Design fidelity against Figma node `40002536:7957`** — no visual checkpoint is evidenced by either the Orchestrator or Tester, and I have no working Figma tool access in this session (the generic MCP capability blurb in my environment did not correspond to an actual callable function here — only `Read`/`Bash` were available to me). This axis stays UNVERIFIED; it needs an actual Storybook-vs-Figma-node comparison recorded before this step can be called fully done, independent of the code fixes below.
- **Real assistive-technology behaviour** for finding #4 (whether a screen reader announces the static `aria-label` during a touch swipe that never moves focus) — jsdom can't exercise this and I have no device to test on, same limitation the Tester hit.
- I did not re-run the Tester's live plant-and-revert mutation for finding #2 end-to-end; I verified the same conclusion structurally from the guard's source instead, which I'm confident is equivalent but is a different method.
- I only have the Tester's paraphrase of the Implementer's self-report (finding #7), not the original text — I can only confirm the shipped code doesn't match what's paraphrased.

## Defects — instruction for this round

**Scope constraint, explicit: stay inside the same 5 files already in this step's manifest. Do not touch `recipeGuards.test.ts` or `recipeParts.test.ts`, do not extract a `ZimmSlideDot` atom, do not restructure the recipe's styling mechanism. All three fixes below are single-line/single-phrase edits.**

1. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSlideIndicator/zimmSlideIndicator.css.ts:48` — 🟡 CONFIRMED. Change `background: isActive ? 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)' : 'var(--zimm-color-opacity-40)'` so the active branch uses `var(--zimm-color-bg-05)` instead of `var(--zimm-color-text-default)`. Both resolve to identical `grey[900]`/`#191919`, so this is a zero-visual-diff change — it swaps a `text.*` token for the semantically correct `bg.*` token on a `background` property, matching `footer.css.ts:33`'s precedent. Do not also touch `zimmButton.css.ts:42`'s identical pattern — that's a separate, pre-existing file outside this step's manifest.

2. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSlideIndicator/index.stories.tsx:5` — 🟡 CONFIRMED. Change `title: 'Elements/ZimmSlideIndicator'` to `title: 'Commerce/ZimmSlideIndicator'`, matching every other PDP-adjacent sibling in this tree per `.claude/rules/components.md`'s categorisation table.

3. Three comments citing an unreachable external plan document — 🟡 CONFIRMED:
   - `index.tsx:26` — `(SFCC-236 plan §4a)`
   - `index.test.tsx:91` — `(sole position signal on touch, see plan §4a)`
   - `zimmSlideIndicator.css.ts:27` — `(SFCC-236 plan §4)`

   Drop the "plan §…" fragment from each — the surrounding prose already states the resolved rationale on its own — or replace it with a bare `(SFCC-236)` Jira reference if you want a ticket anchor. Do not cite a section number of a document nobody outside this build session can open; match the existing citation style already used elsewhere in this codebase (`testing.md §Layer-2`, Handover `button.md §focus`, `TSD §12.1`), all of which point at something a repo-only or company-wide reader can actually reach.

**Explicitly deferred, not this round's job** (report to Marcel, don't fix here):

- Finding #2 (double-`useMultiStyleConfig` test-harness blind spot, 🔴 per Tester) — real and confirmed by me independently, but it's a pre-existing shared-infrastructure gap (same shape already latent in `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts`'s `selected` prop), not a live incorrect value in shipped code, and its real fix (atom extraction or broadening the shared guards) is out of a 4-file step's scope. Recommend a follow-up ticket; worth noting to whoever picks it up that switching the recipe to Chakra `variants` may close it more cheaply than either option the Tester considered.
- Finding #4 (static `aria-label`, not a live region) — PLAUSIBLE, explicitly beyond the letter of the step's pass criteria, unverifiable in jsdom.
- Finding #6 (no `rerender()` case) and #7 (self-report overstatement) — notes only, no action needed.

## Round tracking

This is round 1 of 3 for this step. The three required fixes are small and unambiguous — I'd expect round 2 to close them out, provided the Design Fidelity visual checkpoint against `40002536:7957` also gets recorded before the step is called done.
